title: ISP DNS and Public Resolvers Need a Local Comparison

cover.subtitle: Test your connection and preserve a rollback path.
cover.visual: Two resolver routes connect to a neutral local test checklist.

sections.name: 01-path
sections.heading: Resolver choice changes the lookup operator and its dependencies
sections.scene: A laptop sends DNS through a router to an ISP resolver or an alternative public resolver. No speed winner appears.
sections.alt: A device can reach an ISP resolver or a public resolver.

sections.name: 02-privacy
sections.heading: Privacy depends on the operator and the actual transport
sections.scene: A transport lock protects the network link while a separate resolver-policy card remains visible at the endpoint.
sections.alt: Transport encryption and resolver policy answer different privacy questions.

sections.name: 03-test
sections.heading: A local test compares reliability and useful tasks before speed claims
sections.scene: A neutral comparison worksheet records correct answers, failures, cache state, and application checks without numerical performance scores.
sections.alt: A local test checks answer quality and useful tasks.

sections.name: 04-rollout
sections.heading: A reversible rollout protects local services and future troubleshooting
sections.scene: One test laptop changes settings while other devices retain the baseline, with a clear restore arrow.
sections.alt: A single-device rollout preserves a documented rollback path.

purpose: Initial illustration plan. The final image review manifest records actual asset hashes and visual revisions.
